records.claim: The sr feature integrates into the statistical corrector of TAGE-SC-L to capture correlations between register values and branch directions.
records.quote: We extended the SC with components that capture correlations between register values and branch outcomes. The components use digests of currently available register values as their input.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly describes extending the SC with components correlating register values to branch outcomes.

records.claim: The specification models the RUNLTS register-value-aware predictor published in CBP 2025.
records.quote: RUNLTS: Register-value-aware Predictor Utilizing Nested Large Tables
records.why: The title matches the publication name in the paper.

records.claim: At decode of an instruction writing an architectural register, the predictor records the ROB index as a tag and clears the valid bit.
records.quote: At decode, an instruction that writes a register stores its ROB index as a tag in the corresponding entry and clears the valid bit.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that instructions writing a register store their ROB index as a tag at decode time.

records.claim: When an instruction completes execution, the predictor overwrites the RTT payload with the value digest and sets the valid bit.
records.quote: When the instruction completes, we overwrite the payload with the digest of the produced value and set the valid bit.
records.why: Section 4.2 details that instruction completion updates the payload with the digest and sets the valid bit.

records.claim: The host provides decoded instruction count progression to invalidate RTT digests after 256 decoded instructions.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 confirms valid digests expire after 256 subsequent instructions are decoded.

records.claim: The host supplies flushed ROB tags on pipeline squashes to invalidate stale pending reservations in RTT.
records.open_question: How should RTT in-flight reservations be recovered or invalidated on a misprediction squash given Section 5 leaves Tomasulo-table recovery as future work?

records.claim: Total storage budget for the sR component is 53,863 bits (43,008 bits WT, 9,360 bits UT, 1,495 bits RTT).
records.why: Table 3 gives the exact bit formula and 53,863 bit total for the sR component.

records.claim: For condition-code flags, the 4-bit flag value is replicated three times to form the 12-bit digest.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 explicitly defines replicating the 4 flag bits three times for FLAG digests.

records.claim: For integer registers, leading and trailing bit counts saturate at 63 to fit within 6-bit fields.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U3, how are 0..64 identical leading or trailing bits encoded into 6 bits, and how are zeros vs ones distinguished?

records.claim: Floating-point register digests are right-aligned at digest bit 3 leaving bits [2:0] zeroed.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U4, is the FP slice placed at digest[8:3] with [2:0] zeroed, or right-aligned at digest[5:0]?

records.claim: The RTT consists of 65 entries storing valid (1 bit), payload (14 bits), and decay_ctr (8 bits).
records.why: Table 3 auxiliary data specifies { valid (1), payload (14), decay_ctr (8) } x 65 for RTT.

records.claim: The predictor tracks 65 logical registers across 8 banks.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that the component tracks eight or nine registers per bank across eight banks (8*7 + 9 = 65).

records.claim: An INT value of 0 produces leading and trailing bit counts saturated at 63.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U3, does an all-zero 64-bit value saturate leading/trailing counts at 63 or wrap modulo 64 to 0?

records.claim: An INT register with value 8 produces digest 0x3E3 via XOR folding of trailing count, leading count, and value LSBs.
records.quote: bit 5 |  trailing one/zero #   | bit 0
records.why: Figure 6(a) LITERAL specifies XOR folding of trailing [5:0], leading [8:3], and value LSBs [11:6], evaluating to 3 ^ (60 << 3) ^ (8 << 6) = 0x3E3.

records.claim: A FLAG register with value 0b1011 produces 0xBBB by replicating the 4 bits three times.
records.quote: (3) For condition-code flags, we replicate the four flag bits three times to fill the 12-bit digest.
records.why: Section 4.2 establishes 3-fold replication of 4 flag bits yielding 0xBBB for input 11.

records.claim: An FP32 value places Val[31:26] at digest[8:3] with digest[2:0] zeroed.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U4, does FP32 extraction align at bit 3 leaving bits [2:0] zeroed, or right-align at bit 0?

records.claim: An RTT entry expires and clears valid after 256 consecutive instructions without update.
records.quote: Consequently, RUNLTS invalidates each digest after 256 subsequent instructions have been decoded, ensuring that only up-to-date information influences future predictions.
records.why: Section 4.2 specifies that digests invalidate after 256 subsequent instructions are decoded.

records.claim: A bank with non-positive usefulness selects multiplier x0 and contributes 0 to sR.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U2, is the bank multiplier x0 vs x2.5 driven dynamically per bank by the sign of best_usefulness or statically globally?

records.claim: A bank with positive usefulness selects multiplier x2.5.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U2, is the x2.5 multiplier driven by bank usefulness being positive or a global scale?

records.claim: When multiple registers are valid in a bank during update, one is chosen at random.
records.quote: If several registers were available within the same bank, it randomly selects one of them for the update.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that training randomly selects one available register per bank.

records.claim: The predictor selects the most useful valid register in each bank using the sum of UT0, UT1, and UT2 weights.
records.quote: Unlike the existing components, this component picks the digest of the most useful register among those available and forwards it to the second table.
records.why: Section 4.2 describes selecting the most useful available register in each bank to forward to the weight tables.

records.claim: The bank sum multiplier selects x2.5 if best_usefulness > 0 and x0 otherwise.
records.open_question: Per ambiguity U2, what signal drives the x0 vs x2.5 multiplier selection for each bank?

records.claim: Usefulness tables have 8 entries per bank across 3 tables storing 6-bit weights for all registers in each bank.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL specifies 8-entry tables UT0, UT1, and UT2 with 6-bit weights per register.

records.claim: Prediction table WT0 has 8 banks of 512 entries storing 6-bit signed weights totaling 24,576 bits.
records.why: Table 3 allocates 6 bits x 2^9 entries x 8 banks = 24,576 bits for WT0.

records.claim: Prediction table WT1 has 8 banks of 256 entries storing 6-bit signed weights totaling 12,288 bits.
records.why: Table 3 allocates 6 bits x 2^8 entries x 8 banks = 12,288 bits for WT1.

records.claim: Prediction table WT2 has 8 banks of 128 entries storing 6-bit signed weights totaling 6,144 bits.
records.why: Table 3 allocates 6 bits x 2^7 entries x 8 banks = 6,144 bits for WT2.

records.claim: The register component uses 8 banks.
records.quote: This component is organized into eight banks, each corresponding to eight or nine logical registers.
records.why: Section 4.2 states that the component is organized into eight banks.

records.claim: Table WT0 has 512 entries per bank.
records.why: Table 3 specifies 2^9 (512) entries per bank for WT0.

records.claim: Table WT1 has 256 entries per bank.
records.why: Table 3 specifies 2^8 (256) entries per bank for WT1.

records.claim: Table WT2 has 128 entries per bank.
records.why: Table 3 specifies 2^7 (128) entries per bank for WT2.

records.claim: Each usefulness table has 8 entries per bank.
records.quote: Three usefulness tables: "9x6bit 8 ent. UT0", "8 ent. UT1", "8 ent. UT2".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL specifies 8 entries each for UT0, UT1, and UT2.

records.claim: The bank scaling factor applied to useful predictions is 2.5.
records.quote: That Sigma feeds a multiplier stage labelled "x0 or x2.5".
records.why: Figure 5(c) LITERAL explicitly labels the multiplier stage as x0 or x2.5.
